article.name: GoodAI LTM
article.summary: GoodAI LTM is a Python library for text-based long-term memory and conversational agents. Its low-level memory stores a bounded stream of tokenized text chunks, indexes their embeddings, and retrieves relevant passages; optional models can rewrite queries or memories and rerank retrieved candidates. The repository also includes LTMAgent, which layers dialog and knowledge-base behavior over the memory library.

who_what.text: The official repository describes GoodAI-LTM as a Python package maintained under the GoodAI organization. It offers a low-level text-memory API and an LTMAgent integration; no individual maintainer identity is inferred from commit/profile metadata.

architecture.text: AutoTextMemory.create constructs DefaultTextMemory with a tokenizer, embedding model, bounded ChunkQueue, and simple vector database by default; FAISS flat L2 and optional matching, reranking, rewrite and importance models are configurable.

Chunks carry integer ids, token bounds, metadata, importance, timestamps, indexed length and associated text keys. The queue stores token ids and key-to-sequence mappings, applies overlap and section boundaries, and drops oldest chunks after capacity is exceeded. Default settings are 24 tokens per chunk, 50,000 chunks and 50% overlap.

The simple database retains NumPy vectors and ids and computes squared L2 distances. Explicit persistence APIs serialize the queue and vector database to JSON, JSON plus NPZ, or a state string; the factory alone creates an in-process memory.

behavior.text: add_text accepts text, arbitrary metadata, optional rewrite settings and a timestamp, then returns an integer text key. The implementation tokenizes text, updates queue chunks, and embeds changed chunks in batches; add_separator prevents expansion across section boundaries.

replace_text is exposed as keyed mutation and routes through the chunk-queue operation used by DefaultTextMemory. It is an in-memory replacement interface; the reviewed source does not describe a versioned correction ledger or automatic transactional persistence.

delete_text removes text by returned key; the official example also deletes every text key attached to a retrieved memory. clear resets the whole queue and vector index. The inspected API/example do not document deletion receipts, tombstones, audit records or backup-erasure guarantees.

retrieve(query, k) returns ranked passages with timestamp, distance, relevance, optional matching confidence and importance, metadata and associated keys. Retrieval embeds queries, finds vector candidates, removes duplicate chunks, expands adjacent context within limits, then optionally applies matching/reranking and overlap reduction.

metrics.evidence: Embedding retrieval and optional matching/reranking are implemented; no answer set or abstention behavior was scored.
Keyed replacement exists; no correction sequence or stale-value probe was run.
Keyed deletion and full clear are exposed; no post-delete probe or durable erasure audit was run.
The low-level API and chunk model contain no scope key; no cross-user workload was run.
Metadata and text keys are returned; no claims or citations were adjudicated.
Search and indexing code were inspected; no timings or write-to-recall schedule were measured.
Token chunk limits and persistence formats were inspected; no workload token, cost, or storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: The default memory is an in-process bounded queue; retaining it across process restarts requires caller-managed state or persistence. The simple vector database performs dense pairwise distance calculations over retained vectors, and corpus-scale performance was not measured.

The low-level APIs and chunk records carry no tenant/project/session scope field. Timestamps and arbitrary metadata can carry caller-defined references, but the inspected code does not define verified source provenance or citation support.

This was a pinned source review only. The library, tests and benchmarks were not run; answer quality, abstention, correction, deletion leakage, isolation, latency, tokens, cost and storage remain unmeasured.

benchmark.note: No GoodAI LTM runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run for this review. Source observations and project evaluation definitions are not results measured here.
